params.title: fix(gh): return whole gh.api responses and name cut-short methods
params.msg:
fix(gh): return whole gh.api responses and name cut-short methods

- gh.api captures up to 4 MB (the program-data budget) by default, so JSON responses parse;
  the 50 KB tool-output default cut them mid-document
- gh.api explains process options passed where its flag array belongs
- injection hints list the methods that extend a cut-short name (gh.pr -> gh.prCreate, ...)
  first, ahead of near misses in other namespaces

Refs #379
params.body:
Refs #379 (area: `gh` globals and injection hints).

**gh.api truncated JSON (5 failed calls, plus a regex workaround).** `gh.api` used the default 50 KB stream budget, so larger responses (`compare`, `pulls?per_page=4`) were cut mid-document and `JSON.parse(r.stdout)` failed with `unexpected token: 'web'` and similar (372#6, 375#5, 376#2, 376#6, 376#7). `runtime.completedCalls` returned the same cut-off value, so the suggested recovery didn't help. I reproduced it: the compare of `v2.5.1...v2.5.2` gave 50,944 bytes with `truncated: true`. Now `gh.api` defaults to the program-data budget (4 MB, 1,000,000 lines); a caller's `maxBytes`/`maxLines` still win.

**gh.api misplaced options (375#21).** `api(endpoint, { method, fields })` failed with a bare `args must be an array of strings`. The error now gives a flag example and says that process options go in the third argument.

**`gh.pr` guesses (370#8, 372#43, 375#6).** The hint said `Did you mean: pr, ci, gh?`, which pointed at the project `pr` namespace. Methods whose names start with the missing name now come first, both in `Did you mean` and in the bounded `gh has:` listing, so `gh.pr` points at `prCreate`, `prList`, `prMerge`, and `prView`.

Tests: `gh.api` default and override budgets, the misplaced-options error, and the cut-short-method hint. The session-override test now asserts that the caller's option reaches `execFile`, not the exact options object. `npm run check` and the test suite pass (`delivery.validate`).
